text: cross-platform-sync.mjs reuses a stale debug Tauri binary: its bootstrap phase rebuilds the frontend but not the Rust workspace, so after editing a crate the harness silently tests the OLD binary (bootstrap 87ms vs 22s). A red-proof looked green until I rebuilt with 'cargo tauri build --debug --no-bundle' by hand. The harness should either rebuild the binary or refuse to run when target/debug/futo-notes-tauri is older than the newest crates/ source.

MCP webview_execute_js kills scripts at a short, undocumented timeout (~10s), so any in-app measurement loop must be chunked across calls; the error is a bare 'Script execution timeout' with no hint of the limit. Documenting the ceiling (or accepting a timeout arg) would have saved three failed runs while benchmarking tab switching.

vitest's config restricts include to src/**/*.test.ts, so a throwaway benchmark or probe kept in the scratchpad cannot be run without either a custom config plus a node_modules symlink, or copying the file into src/ and remembering to delete it. Copying into src/ risks leaving a stray test behind (M16). A 'scratch' include glob pointing at the session scratchpad, or a documented one-liner config, would make temporary probes safe.

Playwright test-results/ artifacts from a failing run are wiped by the next passing run of the same spec, so a failure you want to diagnose is gone the moment you re-run to check flakiness. Consider --output to a per-run directory, or preserving error-context.md across runs.

Uploading MR media via glab: 'glab api -F file=@path' returns 400 (that flag JSON-encodes the string '@path'); multipart file upload needs '--form file=@path'. Also, glab api run outside a repo dir silently targets gitlab.com and 401s — run it from the worktree or pass --hostname.

gate-redproofs' GREEN direction runs against committed state, so a NEW untracked file (a skill's references/evidence.md) makes the agent-docs gate report 'green-not-clean / path does not exist' — which reads as a real broken reference in your working tree, where check-agent-docs is clean. Naming the untracked file, or hinting 'commit new files first', would have saved a diagnostic cycle.

docs/perf/tab-switch-baseline.md told agents to seed a perf corpus by rsyncing ~/Documents/futo-notes (real user data) into the machine-global ~/Documents/fake-notes — two hard AGENTS.md prohibitions in one code block, and parallel sessions share that path. Fixed to generate into the worktree's .tauri-data; a doc that hands out a banned command is worse than no doc.

scripts/perf/tab-switch-probe.js hung forever whenever the app window was occluded: WebKit suspends requestAnimationFrame, so an await raf() never resolves and the probe looked stuck rather than blocked. A QA leg reported the perf claim BLOCKED because of this. Added check()/framesLive() so it says 'frames are stalled' in ~1.2s.

No documented way to bring a dev Tauri window forward for a frame-dependent probe: core:window:allow-set-focus is denied to the webview and OS input automation is banned. Launching a second copy of the same debug binary works (tauri-plugin-single-instance calls window.set_focus() from Rust, ungated) — cost me ~30min to find; now in the probe header + /verify desktop reference.

check-agent-docs.mjs does not scan .claude/agents/**, so a subagent definition (app-qa.md) can carry a stale command, a broken path, or an unsafe technique that every repo gate steps over — the app-qa agent's QA instructions were invisible to the docs gate while it drove real apps

22 skill symlinks under .claude/skills/ pointed into the gitignored .agents/, so every slash command they provided (/tdd, /research, /wayfinder, ...) was dead in every git worktree and fresh clone while looking fine in the primary checkout. check-agent-docs could not see it because readdir() reports a symlink as neither file nor directory, so the subtree was skipped. Prevented by: check-agent-docs now failing on a tracked skill symlink whose target is missing or untracked (added in !211), plus 'just skills-link' for the local links.

scripts/gate-redproofs.mjs revert() ran only 'git checkout -- .' + 'git clean -fd', neither of which touches the index, so a red-proof whose violation only exists once git TRACKS the path (a committed symlink) could not be written: the staged entry survived revert and tripped the cleanliness assertion for the next proof. Prevented by: revert() now 'git reset -q' first (added in !211).

scripts/ci-cargo-cache-freshness.test.mjs flakes under machine load: it fails inside the parallel test:unit:full run (1-6 of its 15 cases, count varies run to run) but passes 15/15 when run alone. Reproduced identically on a pristine origin/main worktree, so it is not branch-specific. It shells out to git in temp repos, so it is presumably racing other git activity / hitting its own timing assumptions when several agents share the machine. Blocks 'just check' for anyone doing parallel work. Prevented by: waiting on conditions instead of wall-clock in that test (M15), or serializing it.

tests/cross-platform-sync.mjs has no per-worktree isolation: server ports are a fixed 4000+ counter and the Postgres reset goes through the machine-global docker compose 'futo-notes-postgres' with a TRUNCATE of the shared futo_notes DB. Two worktrees running the harness at once collide on both. Slot-derive the base port (scripts/lib/slot.mjs) and the database name like scripts/qa.mjs already does.

The harness's FUTO_NOTES_E2EE_DATABASE_URL escape hatch (tests/lib/sync-test-server.mjs) shells out to a host psql, which is not installed on this Mac (Postgres runs only in the compose container), so opting into an isolated database fails with the generic 'Failed to reset E2EE server database'. Either run the reset through 'docker compose exec' with the given URL or say psql is required.

the house main-guard pattern `import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href` throws ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE when the module is imported from `node -e`/`node --eval` (argv[1] undefined), so ad-hoc classification checks against an exported helper crash before running — needs `process.argv[1] &&`; present in several scripts/*.mjs

tests/lib/tauri-instance.mjs and tests/cross-platform-sync.mjs resolve the debug binary as <repoRoot>/target/debug/futo-notes-tauri and ignore $CARGO_TARGET_DIR, so a relocated target dir makes the suite die with ENOENT AFTER a successful 84-second build. Honouring CARGO_TARGET_DIR (cargo prints 'Built application at:' with the real path) would have prevented it; scripts/remote-test.mjs now carries a REPO_LOCAL_TARGET_RECIPES exception list instead.

tests/lib/sync-test-server.mjs shells out to 'bun src/index.ts hash' but nothing documents or checks that bun must be on PATH, and the failure is 'Failed to hash test server password:\nundefined' — result.stderr and result.stdout are both undefined when spawnSync cannot find the binary, so the message names neither bun nor ENOENT. Reporting result.error would have pointed straight at it.

scripts/check-agent-docs.mjs crashes with ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE when imported from a context where process.argv[1] is undefined (node -e / node --input-type=module): its entry guard calls pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]) unguarded. Other scripts in the repo guard with 'process.argv[1] &&' first.

scripts/ci-cargo-cache-freshness.test.mjs inherits the caller's $CARGO_TARGET_DIR: the guard resolves TARGET_DIR from that env var, so with it set the tests inspect a directory that does not exist, the guard reports 'no restored target/' and exits 0, and 5 tests fail asserting exit 1. Green on a normal Mac, red under any runner that sets CARGO_TARGET_DIR (this is how it surfaced). The test should pass CARGO_TARGET_DIR: undefined in its runGuard env, the way it already pins CI_PROJECT_DIR.

tests/cross-platform-sync.mjs dies with 'Could not connect to ws://127.0.0.1:9223' when a Chromium browser (Brave, --remote-debugging-port=9223) is running: the MCP bridge plugin binds 0.0.0.0:9223 successfully because the browser only holds 127.0.0.1:9223, logs that port as its own, and the harness's ws:// connect then reaches the BROWSER. Workaround is to occupy 0.0.0.0:9223 yourself so the plugin scans up to 9224. Would have been prevented by the plugin binding 127.0.0.1 (or the app taking a slot-derived base port) and by the harness naming the port holder in that error.

tests/cross-platform-sync.mjs only rebuilt the desktop binary when it was MISSING, so a second mesh run in the same checkout silently tested the previous run's binary — a #89 fix got a byte-identical false red with 'bootstrap 19ms'. Fixed in this branch by rebuilding when any embedded source is newer than the binary; the general lesson is that any harness caching a built artifact needs a source-staleness check, not just an existence check.

prettier --check enforces BROKEN markdown in docs/spec/sync.md: a blockquoted Gap containing a code span that wraps across lines (`just / journal --dir`) is reformatted so the continuation line loses its '> ' marker and sits at column 0, which stops being a blockquote. A merge that restores the correct '  > journal --dir' fails format:check, so the only way to be green is to keep the broken form. Would have been prevented by not wrapping a code span across a blockquote line, or a prettier ignore range there.
